title: Knowledge check: Migration Strategies

questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “Migration Strategies” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Maintaining the existing application temporarily” under lesson 114, “Migration Strategies”. The distractors belong to other lesson topics.

questions.prompt: When applying “Migration Strategies” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Assume a backup is valid without a restoration test.
Migrate every feature in one unmeasured cutover.
Record assumptions, compare behavior with acceptance criteria, and define rollback.
Skip tests if the code compiles.
questions.answer_key: Record assumptions, compare behavior with acceptance criteria, and define rollback.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps migration strategies testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “Migration Strategies” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.
